prompt: In the network shown, C1 = 3 uF sits alone in the upper branch while C2 = 6 uF and C3 = 2 uF sit one after the other in the lower branch, both branches spanning the same two terminals A and B. Calculate (a) the equivalent capacitance and (b) the total charge stored when connected to a 24 V battery.

figure.alt: Between terminals A and B, an upper branch carries C1 of 3 microfarads alone, and a lower branch carries C2 of 6 microfarads followed by C3 of 2 microfarads in series. The two branches are in parallel with each other.
figure.caption: Tutorial slide 3

explanation: Work from the inside of the picture outwards. C2 and C3 sit one after the other with no junction between them, so they are in SERIES: 1/Cs = 1/6 + 1/2 = 1/6 + 3/6 = 4/6, giving Cs = 6/4 = 1.5 uF. That branch and C1 both run from A to B, sharing the same two ends, so they are in PARALLEL and simply add: C = 3 + 1.5 = 4.5 uF. Then the charge, Q = CV = 4.5 x 10^-6 x 24 = 1.08 x 10^-4 C, which is 108 uC. Two guards catch the wrong routes: a series combination must come out SMALLER than its smallest member, and 1.5 is duly under 2; and adding in parallel can only INCREASE the total, so the answer must exceed 3.

why.a: Correct. Series pair first, 1.5 uF, then parallel with C1 gives 4.5 uF, and Q = CV = 4.5 x 24 = 108 uC.
why.b: No. 11 uF is 3 + 6 + 2, which treats all three as parallel. C2 and C3 have a junction only between themselves, which is what series means.
why.c: No. 1.5 uF is the series pair on its own, so this stops one step early and never adds C1.
why.d: No. The capacitance is right but the charge is not: Q = CV needs the 24 V, and 4.5 uC is the capacitance with a C stuck on it.
why.e: No. 0.92 uF is what treating all three as series would give, which is smaller than every capacitor present and therefore impossible here.

prompt: In the network shown, C1 = 6 uF sits alone in the upper branch while C2 = 3 uF and C3 = 6 uF sit one after the other in the lower branch; that whole block is then in series with C5 = 12 uF on the way to B. Calculate (a) the equivalent capacitance and (b) the total charge supplied by a 48 V battery.

figure.alt: Between A and B, a parallel block has C1 of 6 microfarads alone in its upper branch and C2 of 3 microfarads in series with C3 of 6 microfarads in its lower branch. That block is then in series with C5 of 12 microfarads before reaching B.
figure.caption: Tutorial slide 4, first network

explanation: Three steps, innermost first. C2 and C3 are in series: 1/Cs = 1/3 + 1/6 = 2/6 + 1/6 = 3/6, so Cs = 2 uF. That branch is in parallel with C1, so Cp = 6 + 2 = 8 uF. Finally Cp is in series with C5, which is the lecturer's own line on the slide, 1/CT = 1/8 + 1/12 = 3/24 + 2/24 = 5/24, giving CT = 24/5 = 4.8 uF. Then Q = CV = 4.8 x 10^-6 x 48 = 2.304 x 10^-4 C, which is 230.4 uC. Notice the shape of the work: series, then parallel, then series again, always collapsing the group you can already name.

why.a: Correct. 2 uF for the series pair, 8 uF after the parallel step, 4.8 uF after the final series step, and Q = 4.8 x 48 = 230.4 uC.
why.b: No. 8 uF is the parallel block before C5 is brought in, so this stops one step early.
why.c: No. 27 uF is 6 + 3 + 6 + 12, which treats the whole network as parallel and ignores the picture entirely.
why.d: No. 2 uF is the C2 and C3 series pair alone, which is only the first of three steps.
why.e: No. 20 uF is 8 + 12, adding C5 in parallel when it plainly sits one after the block, which is series.

prompt: In the network shown, C1 = 4 uF and C2 = 8 uF sit side by side between the same two points, and that pair is then in series with C3 = 5 uF. Calculate (a) the equivalent capacitance and (b) the total energy stored when connected to a 30 V source.

figure.alt: Between A and B, C1 of 4 microfarads and C2 of 8 microfarads sit one above the other between the same two nodes, so they are in parallel. That pair is then in series with C3 of 5 microfarads before reaching B.
figure.caption: Tutorial slide 4, second network

explanation: C1 and C2 span the same two nodes, so they are in PARALLEL and add: Cp = 4 + 8 = 12 uF. That pair then sits one after C3, which is SERIES: 1/CT = 1/12 + 1/5 = 5/60 + 12/60 = 17/60, so CT = 60/17 = 3.53 uF. For the energy, U = 1/2 CV^2 = 0.5 x 3.53 x 10^-6 x 30^2 = 0.5 x 3.53 x 10^-6 x 900 = 1.59 x 10^-3 J, which is 1.59 mJ. The V is SQUARED, which is the step most often dropped; forgetting it would give 0.053 mJ, and forgetting the half would give 3.18 mJ.

why.a: Correct. 12 uF in parallel, 3.53 uF after the series step, and U = 1/2 x 3.53 uF x 900 = 1.59 mJ.
why.b: No. 17 uF is 4 + 8 + 5, treating the whole network as parallel, which ignores that C3 sits after the pair rather than beside it.
why.c: No. 12 uF is the parallel pair before C3 is brought in, so this stops one step early.
why.d: No. The capacitance is right but the energy is halved: 0.79 mJ is what you get by using 1/2 CV^2 with a half applied twice, or by using 15 V.
why.e: No. 1.74 uF is roughly what treating all three as series would give, which must be smaller than the smallest capacitor and is therefore not this network.
